guides.definition: Loads selected CSV columns into a DataFrame and filters rows with a boolean condition. Requires pandas and any file-format engine used by the snippet in the selected Python environment; Hypershell does not install them.

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: Columns to load from the file.

parameters.name: filterColumn
parameters.description: Column used by the row condition.

parameters.name: filterValue
parameters.description: Value compared with the selected column.

examples.title: Load active users
examples.code:
import pandas as pd

frame = pd.read_csv("users.csv", usecols=["id", "name", "active"])
filtered = frame.loc[frame["active"] == True]
examples.explanation: usecols avoids loading unused data; loc keeps the row-filter operation explicit and chainable.

guides.definition: Groups a DataFrame by one column and computes a named aggregate for another. Requires pandas and any file-format engine used by the snippet in the selected Python environment; Hypershell does not install them.

parameters.name: groupColumn
parameters.description: Column whose distinct values define groups.

parameters.name: outputColumn
parameters.description: Name for the aggregated result column.

parameters.name: aggregate
parameters.description: Aggregate name such as sum, mean, or count.

examples.title: Total sales by region
examples.explanation: Named aggregation gives the result column a stable name while making the source column and operation visible.

guides.definition: Merges two DataFrames on a named key with an explicit join strategy. Requires pandas and any file-format engine used by the snippet in the selected Python environment; Hypershell does not install them.

parameters.name: joinType
parameters.description: Merge strategy such as inner, left, right, or outer.

parameters.name: validation
parameters.description: Expected key relationship checked by pandas.

examples.title: Join users to departments
